positives.title: Hello, I’m Anna!
positives.originalText:
Jonathan: Hey, Pete! Who’s your friend?
Pete: She is Anna. She is new to D.C.
Jonathan: Where are you from?
Anna: I am from a small town.
Jonathan: Well, welcome to D.C.
Anna: Thank you.
Jonathan: I am Jonathan. I am in apartment B4.
Anna: I am in apartment C2. Marsha is my roommate.
Jonathan: I know Marsha. She is nice.
Pete: And I am in Apartment D7. I have to go now.
Anna: Oh!
Pete: Remember to call Marsha at work. Tell her you’re here.
Anna: Right, thanks, Pete. Nice to meet you!

positives.title: Lesson 16: Where Are You From?
positives.originalText:
Anna: Hello! Washington, D.C. has many tourists! People from different countries come here. Today, my job is to interview tourists. I have to learn why they come here. This is very exciting! Excuse me. I’m Anna Matteo from The News. Do you have time for an interview?

Sabrina: Sure, I have time.

Anna: What is your name?

Sabrina: My name is Sabrina.

Anna: What country are you from?

Sabrina: I’m from Bangladesh.

Anna: So, you are Bangladeshi.

Sabrina: That’s right! My nationality is Bangladeshi.

Anna: Do you like Washington, D.C.?

Sabrina: Yes! The city is very beautiful!

Anna: What do you like to do in Washington D.C.?

Sabrina: I like history. So, I like walking around and looking at all the monuments and memorials. They make history come alive!

Anna: Washington has many monuments and memorials. The Washington Monument is behind us! Which is your favorite?

Sabrina: I really like Lincoln Memorial. It is very beautiful. And it feels like Abraham Lincoln is still alive.

Anna: Awesome. Thank you for your time, Sabrina!

Sabrina: You’re welcome.

Anna: Let’s find another tourist.

Anna: Oh! Excuse me. I am Anna Matteo from The News. Do you have time for a couple of questions?

Louis: Sure!

Anna: Are you from Washington, D.C.?

Louis: No, I’m not.

Anna: What is your name and where are you from?

Louis: My name is Louis. And I’m from China.

Anna: What languages do you speak?

Louis: I speak Chinese and English.

Anna: What do you like about Washington DC?

Louis: I like the museums. I really like the art museums.

Anna: Many of the museums are free.

Louis: I like that too!

Anna: Awesome! Thanks for your time, Louis.

Louis: You’re very welcome. Bye!

Anna: Now, let’s find another tourist!

Anna: Hello! I am Anna Matteo from The News. Do you have time to answer a couple of questions?

Mehrnoush: Sure!

Anna: What is your name and where’re you from?

Mehrnoush: My name is Mehrnoush. I am from Iran. I’m Iranian.

Anna: What language do they speak in Iran? Is it Persian?

Mehrnoush: They speak Farsi.

Anna: What do you like to do in Washington DC?

Mehrnoush: Well, I like learning about government and politics.

Anna: Washington has many politicians!

Mehrnoush: It does! I want to see the U.S. Capitol.

Anna: Look, you are very near.

Mehrnoush: I am!

Anna: Have fun!

Mehrnoush: Thanks!

Anna: There you have it. Tourists from all over the world come to Washington, D.C. They all like doing and seeing different things in the city. This is Anna Matteo reporting for The News. Until next time!

Anna: Is that okay? Awesome! Now, I want to do my favorite thing in the city … ride the carousel!

semanticDesign.incorrectReason: The retained Louis interview includes Anna’s Washington, D.C. origin question and Louis’s explicit “No, I’m not.” The later direct answer states China. His liking Washington museums supplies visit context, not residence or origin. Anna’s “from The News” is professional affiliation and must not be accepted as an origin answer.
semanticDesign.reviewDecision: Suitable source evidence for a new generator-type design and automated rule validation. No generated question instance approved or required.

transferBoundary.sameSemanticOperation: Retrieve the explicitly stated self-origin in response to a direct origin question; distinguish it from another place named in the same dialogue.
transferBoundary.A1: Only the Anna root has existing A1 support, so this does not establish A1 transfer. Do not broaden Louis support or treat repeated passages of one root as transfer.

minimalClientRuleDesign.inputs: Only an already-supported intact passage with actual speaker turns and valid source/rights/exclusions. Preserve the Louis Washington question/No response and the complete 106-word interview.
minimalClientRuleDesign.recognition: Require a complete direct Where are you from? or What is your name and where are you from? turn by a different speaker immediately before the positive first-person origin turn. The latter may contain a complete My name is NAME. prefix only if NAME agrees with the actual speaker label. Accept a single complete I am from PLACE. / I’m from PLACE. proposition, optional And; reject modal, negation, conditional, temporal, reported/quoted or multiple-origin claims. Do not search free occurrences of from or resolve she/he/it to people.
minimalClientRuleDesign.options: One exact origin phrase and one distinct exact source-place distractor. Obtain the latter from an immediately subsequent welcome-to place, or an immediately preceding asked-origin question plus the target person’s explicit No, I’m not. followed by the actual origin question/answer. For the negative question branch preserve both question and denial. Never treat a question or a negative answer as a positive origin statement; reject missing or ambiguous denial. No invented place or organization option.
minimalClientRuleDesign.placeBoundaries: A bounded geographical noun phrase in an explicit origin exchange; generic town/city/village phrases or conservative proper place phrases. Reject organizational affiliation (including The News), uncertain/disjunctive phrases and identical answer/distractor. D.C. punctuation must retain its full acronym. The disposable probe’s capitalized-place approximation is feasibility evidence only; a production implementation must validate its full negative boundary, rather than claim arbitrary capitalized names are known geography.
minimalClientRuleDesign.scoring: Use existing choice controls, exact option identities and current saved-answer transaction. Correct/incorrect reflect only the explicit textual fact. Ordinary and generated Test modes may share the snapshot; Test must retain no assistance. Open responses remain unscored. No CEFR claim.
minimalClientRuleDesign.questionBoundary: Ask where PERSON says they are from; never where they were born/live or what nationality/language they have. This is a relation between a named person and their stated origin, not completing the word from or attributing a random turn.
